items.text: Quotients in a category of sheaves

$H\subset G$ a subgroup object: $G/H$ (quotient of the equivalence relation $g\sim gh$, effective in sheaves) with $G$ acting on it by left translations; if $H$ is invariant, $G/H$ is a group. Torsors behave as for sets.
Schemes are sheaves for the fpqc topology: $X(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,X)$.

S''=S'\times_SS'\rightrightarrows S'\to S\ \ (S'\to S\ \text{faithfully flat quasi-compact});\qquad \operatorname{Hom}(S,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(S',X)\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}(S'',X)\ \text{exact}
\operatorname{Hom}_S(Y,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(Y',X')\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}_{S''}(Y'',X'')\quad\text{exact (one-descent); take }Y=S
The topology could be enlarged to all families of universal strict epimorphisms; fpqc morphisms have many further properties. Other topologies:
Faithfully flat of finite presentation (fppf): open coverings plus faithfully flat morphisms locally of finite presentation.

Covering for fpqc: every point of $S$ has an open neighbourhood $S'$ over which the family $S'_i=S_i\times_SS'$ is refined by finitely many $T_\alpha$ with $\coprod T_\alpha\to S'$ quasi-compact and faithfully flat, each $T_\alpha$ factoring through some $S'_i$.

Discrete topology: families with a global section. Zariski: local sections on an open cover. Étale: surjective families of étale morphisms. fppf: families flat and locally of finite presentation, jointly surjective.

No necessary and sufficient criterion for a sheaf to be a scheme. Artin: replace schemes by algebraic spaces (glued for the étale topology instead of the Zariski topology); then a good criterion exists, moduli problems are representable, contractions exist. A compact analytic space with transcendence degree of meromorphic functions equal to its dimension is an algebraic space.
Analogy: algebraic spaces are to schemes as distributions are to functions.
Passage to quotients
$R\rightrightarrows X$ an equivalence relation with $p_1$ (hence $p_2$) faithfully flat quasi-compact. A quotient $Y$ in the category of schemes is satisfactory only if it is the quotient in sheaves:
X\to Y\ \text{faithfully flat quasi-compact},\qquad R=X\times_YX
The quotient sheaf $X/R$ always exists; representability is the delicate point (Mumford, Geometric Invariant Theory).

Theorem. $R$ with $p_1,p_2$ finite and locally free. Then $X/R$ is representable (by $Y$ with $X\to Y$ finite, locally free, $R=X\times_YX$) iff $X$ is a union of affine open sets $X_i$ stable under $R$,
X_i=p_2\bigl(p_1^{-1}(X_i)\bigr)

Equivalent: every equivalence class (finite) lies in an affine open set; automatic if $X$ is quasi-projective over an affine base or carries an ample line bundle. If $X$ is affine the quotient always exists.
A finite group $G$ acting on $X$ without fixed points: $X/G$ is a scheme iff every orbit lies in an affine open set.
$X$, $R$ of finite type over a field, $p_1$ flat: there is a dense open subset of $X$ stable under $R$ with a quotient scheme (Bourbaki seminar, SGA 3; refined: complement of codimension $\ge2$).

$G$ an algebraic group over a field, $H\subset G$ a subgroup: $H$ is flat over $k$, so the equivalence relation is flat; translating a dense open set, $G/H$ exists as a scheme, a homogeneous space of $G$.
Open problems
Equivalence relations that are not flat, e.g. on schemes finite over a field or a noetherian scheme: effective? (i.e. is $R=X\times_{X/R}X$.) Probably not; nobody has tried seriously.
